title: check.py's own-log rule refuses an internal root's own source id in its _logs.csv context, since leak_hits now holds the private names
goal: check.py accepts an internal root's own log row whose context cites its own source id (source:<prefix>-<id>), while a public root's log still refuses a private name

run:
import csv, os, sys, tempfile
d = tempfile.mkdtemp(); r = os.path.join(d, "team-x"); os.makedirs(r)
open(os.path.join(r, "_root.md"), "w").write("---\nroot: team-x\nid_prefix: TX\nvisibility: internal\n---\n\n# team-x\n")
os.environ["KB_ROOTS"] = r
sys.path.insert(0, "_tools")
import check, kbcommon
w = csv.writer(open(os.path.join(r, check.LOGS), "w", newline=""))
w.writerow(check.LOG_COLS)
row = {c: "" for c in check.LOG_COLS}
row.update(id="L-aaaaaaaa", observation="3 runs", context="source:TX-" + "k3f7q2zd", status="current")
w.writerow([row[c] for c in check.LOG_COLS])
del w
root = [x for x in kbcommon.roots() if x.name == "team-x"][0]
check.check_logs(root, {"TX": root}, {"team-x": {"TX-" + "k3f7q2zd"}})
bad = [e for e in check.errors if "private-id" in str(e)]
print(bad)
sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)

import csv, os, sys, tempfile
d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
def mk(name, pre, vis):
    r = os.path.join(d, name); os.makedirs(r)
    open(os.path.join(r, "_root.md"), "w").write(f"---\nroot: {name}\nid_prefix: {pre}\nvisibility: {vis}\n---\n\n# {name}\n")
    return r
rx, rp = mk("team-x", "TX", "internal"), mk("team-p", "TP", "public")
os.environ["KB_ROOTS"] = os.pathsep.join([rx, rp])
sys.path.insert(0, "_tools")
import check, kbcommon
w = csv.writer(open(os.path.join(rp, check.LOGS), "w", newline=""))
w.writerow(check.LOG_COLS)
row = {c: "" for c in check.LOG_COLS}
row.update(id="L-aaaaaaaa", observation="3 runs", context="source:TX-" + "k3f7q2zd", status="current")
w.writerow([row[c] for c in check.LOG_COLS])
del w
root = [x for x in kbcommon.roots() if x.name == "team-p"][0]
check.check_logs(root, {"TX": [x for x in kbcommon.roots() if x.name == "team-x"][0], "TP": root}, {"team-p": set(), "team-x": {"TX-" + "k3f7q2zd"}})
bad = [e for e in check.errors if "private" in str(e) or "leak-scan" in str(e)]
print("errors of the public root's log:", bad)
sys.exit(0 if bad else 1)
